messages.content: What is the largest planet in the universe?

function.name: space_star_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a particular star in the universe. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

information.description: The type of information needed about the star.

message.content:
The largest planet that astronomers have confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**.  
It orbits the young star HD 100546 (about 320 light‑years away in the constellation Musca) and was first imaged in 2014.

| Property | Value |
|----------|-------|
| **Radius** | ≈ 2.5 × Jupiter’s radius (≈ 180,000 km) |
| **Mass** | ≈ 10 × Jupiter’s mass (≈ 3 × 10²⁴ kg) |
| **Orbital distance** | ~ 10–15 AU from its host star |
| **Age of system** | ~ 5–10 million years (very young) |

Because HD 100546 b is still accreting material from its surrounding protoplanetary disk, its size and mass are expected to grow further. In practice, the “largest planet” is a moving target: as new exoplanets are discovered—especially those that are still forming—astronomers may find objects that exceed HD 100546 b’s dimensions.

So, while HD 100546 b is the biggest confirmed planet today, the universe may yet hold even larger worlds that we haven’t detected yet.
